cls: Locally acting chloride channel (ClC-2) activator - laxative / intestinal secretagogue
pharm: A bicyclic fatty acid derived from prostaglandin E1 that locally activates apical ClC-2 chloride channels in the intestine, increasing chloride-rich fluid secretion to soften stool and increase motility without altering serum sodium or potassium.
quick: CIC 24 mcg BID; IBS-C (women) 8 mcg BID; OIC 24 mcg BID
Take with food and water; swallow whole to reduce nausea
Use only if benefit justifies risk (animal fetal loss at high doses)
Caution; monitor a breastfed infant for diarrhea
Reduce dose in moderate (Child-Pugh B) and severe (Child-Pugh C) impairment
Exclude GI obstruction; watch for severe diarrhea, dyspnea, syncope
summary: Lubiprostone (Amitiza) is a locally acting chloride channel (ClC-2) activator approved for chronic idiopathic constipation in adults (24 mcg twice daily), irritable bowel syndrome with constipation in women 18 years and older (8 mcg twice daily), and opioid-induced constipation in adults with chronic non-cancer pain (24 mcg twice daily). It activates apical ClC-2 channels in the intestine, increasing chloride-rich luminal fluid that softens stool and increases motility without altering serum sodium or potassium. It should be taken with food and water and swallowed whole to reduce nausea, its most common adverse effect. It is contraindicated in known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction. Dose reduction is needed in moderate to severe hepatic impairment, while no renal adjustment is required. Lubiprostone is rapidly and extensively metabolized locally in the stomach and jejunum by carbonyl reductase (not by hepatic CYP450), giving low systemic exposure. Its effectiveness in opioid-induced constipation has not been established with diphenylheptane (methadone-class) opioids.
indications: Irritable bowel syndrome with constipation in women 18 years of age and older
Opioid-induced constipation in adults with chronic non-cancer pain

dosage.c: Chronic idiopathic constipation (normal or mild hepatic)

dosage.n: Effectiveness not established with methadone-class opioids; reduce in hepatic impairment as for CIC
No change for mild or moderate hepatic impairment

admin: Take orally with food and water
Swallow capsules whole - do not break or chew
Taking with food reduces the most common adverse effect, nausea
Confirm absence of mechanical GI obstruction before starting
Reassess periodically the need for continued therapy
moa: Lubiprostone is a locally acting chloride channel activator that enhances chloride-rich intestinal fluid secretion without altering serum sodium or potassium concentrations. It specifically activates ClC-2 chloride channels on the apical membrane of the human intestine in a protein-kinase-A-independent fashion. The resulting increase in luminal fluid secretion increases intestinal motility and the passage of stool, thereby relieving constipation. Its activity is primarily local within the gut.

absolute: Known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction
relative: Moderate to severe hepatic impairment (reduce dose)
Conditions in which delayed gastric emptying or dyspnea would be poorly tolerated
Use with diphenylheptane (methadone-class) opioids for OIC (efficacy not established)
monitor: Dyspnea / chest tightness, especially after the first dose

preg: There are no adequate human data. Animal studies in guinea pigs showed dose-dependent fetal loss at 0.2 to 6 times the maximum recommended human dose, without structural malformations. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: It is not known whether lubiprostone is excreted in human milk; it was undetectable in rat milk. Use with caution and monitor a breastfed infant for diarrhea.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in renal impairment.
hepatic: Dose reduction is required in hepatic impairment because of higher exposure to the M3 metabolite. For CIC and OIC, start at 16 mcg twice daily in moderate (Child-Pugh B) and 8 mcg twice daily in severe (Child-Pugh C) impairment. For IBS-C, no change is needed in mild or moderate impairment, but start at 8 mcg once daily in severe (Child-Pugh C) impairment.

major: Diphenylheptane opioids (methadone) - dose-dependently reduce ClC-2 activation and may decrease the efficacy of lubiprostone
moderate: Low likelihood of pharmacokinetic drug interactions because lubiprostone is not metabolized by CYP450 enzymes
interactions.food: Take with food, which reduces nausea; a high-fat meal lowers Cmax by about 55% without affecting overall exposure (AUC).

emergency: Dyspnea, chest tightness, or difficulty breathing occurring 30-60 minutes after a dose

monitoring: Exclude mechanical GI obstruction before starting
Dyspnea / chest tightness, especially after the first dose
counsel: Take each dose with food and water and swallow the capsule whole to reduce nausea
If you develop severe diarrhea, stop the medicine and contact your provider
You may feel short of breath or chest tightness within about an hour of a dose, especially the first dose - this usually passes but report it
This medicine may cause fainting or dizziness; rise slowly
If you are breastfeeding, watch your baby for diarrhea
For IBS-C, this product is approved only for women 18 years and older
pk: First bowel movement often within 24-48 hours
Active metabolite M3 Tmax about 1.1 hours
pearls: Acts locally, so it has few systemic drug interactions and is not CYP-metabolized
Always take with food and water to mitigate nausea, the dose-limiting adverse effect
The IBS-C indication is limited to women 18 years and older
Methadone (and other diphenylheptane opioids) can blunt its efficacy in opioid-induced constipation
Hepatic impairment requires dose reduction, but renal impairment does not; dyspnea/chest tightness can occur 30-60 minutes after a dose and may recur
missed: Not specified in the prescribing information. General guidance: take the missed dose when you remember unless it is near the next dose, in which case skip it; do not double the dose.
overdose: There is no specific antidote, and reported overdoses have generally been benign (a child who ingested 7-8 capsules of 24 mcg fully recovered; 96 mcg/day for 8 days produced no adverse effects). In a phase 1 study at 144 mcg, the most frequent adverse effects were nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, dizziness, and headache. Management is supportive and symptomatic.
